decided: Under the program sign-off, a program counts as finished when each stage it declares is in one of four states: all its work archived and waiting for ratification; complete; ended by the user; or ended because the explorations for it concluded with no change. So a stage the user ended without archiving any change does not stop it. With the setting at its default, the end-of-program readout still asks that every stage be archived, worded as today; the difference between the two for an ended stage is written down as a known limit for the program's next architect session to settle.
alternatives: use the program sign-off's wider test of finished, which counts an ended stage, for the end-of-program readout under every setting, which would change what users see with no setting changed
why: Nothing the user sees may change with every setting at its default, and a program that withdrew a stage must still be able to finish under the program sign-off.
